title: Best Travel Adaptors UK
short: Universal travel adaptors compared by plug compatibility, charging power and safety features, from budget picks to high-power GaN chargers.
intro: A good travel adaptor needs to fit securely, charge fast enough for modern devices, and cover the plug types for wherever you're actually going. This guide compares adaptors tested by T3's travel team, who take each one on real trips charging laptops, phones, cameras and more.

products.name: TA-105 Max World Travel Adapter
products.key_spec: 75W GaN, 3x USB-C + 2x USB-A, charges up to 6 devices, includes carry case
products.summary: T3's top pick, compact yet able to charge up to six devices simultaneously with fast charging on every port. Its sturdy build includes an 8A fuse and safety shutters plus a premium carry case, though it doesn't support Type D or M plugs and can't convert voltage.
cons: Doesn't support Type D or Type M plugs

products.name: OneWorld135
products.best_for: Buyers who need to charge a laptop and several devices at full speed
products.key_spec: 135W GaN, 3x USB-C (2x at 100W) + 1x USB-A, over 200 countries
products.summary: T3 found this capable of charging two MacBook Pros at full speed simultaneously thanks to its two 100W USB-C ports and advanced GaN technology. It's compatible in over 200 countries and charges up to five devices at once, though it lacks a grounding pin.

products.best_for: Budget-conscious travellers who still want fast charging

guide.q: Do I need a voltage converter as well as an adaptor?
guide.a: Not always. A travel adaptor only changes the plug shape to fit a foreign socket, not the voltage. Most modern phones, laptops and cameras are dual voltage (100-240V) and work fine with just an adaptor, but high-powered items like hair dryers or straighteners often aren't dual voltage and may need a separate voltage converter.

guide.q: What plug type do I need for my destination?
guide.a: Plug types are labelled A to N by shape: Type G is the UK's own three-pin plug, Type C is the most common worldwide (used across Europe, South America and Asia), and Type I covers Australia, New Zealand and China. A universal adaptor covering A, C, G and I, like most in this guide, handles the large majority of common destinations.

guide.q: How much charging power (wattage) do I actually need?
guide.a: For phones and most everyday gadgets, 30-75W is plenty, even when charging several devices at once. If you need to charge a laptop at full speed too, look for a higher-wattage adaptor with USB-C Power Delivery, like the OneAdaptr OneWorld135 or VisaPro here, both rated over 100W.

guide.q: What safety features should I look for?
guide.a: Look for a built-in fuse (ideally replaceable), surge protection and safety shutters over unused sockets, all featured on the reputable adaptors in this guide. Avoid very cheap, unbranded adaptors with no clear safety markings, since they can overheat or short out.
